items.title: 2.6.3.3 Indexing and Slicing with Negative Indices

source_refs.note: Topic 2.6.3.3 Indexing and Slicing with Negative Indices (PDF 53-54, printed 50-51), with the class activity.

blocks.text: Negative indices count from the end of a sequence: -1 is the last element, -2 the second last, and so on.

blocks.title: Python code (each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
fruits = ["Apple", "Banana", "Cherry", "Date", "Elderberry"]
print("First fruit:", fruits[0])
print("Last fruit:", fruits[-1])
print(fruits[1:4])    # Banana, Cherry, Date
print(fruits[-4:-1])  # Banana, Cherry, Date

blocks.alt: Top: five fruits in boxes with indexes 0 to 4 above and -5 to -1 below, and the slice from index 1 to 4 marked. Bottom left: main.py importing greetings.py and a package ecommerce with three modules. Bottom right: a ToyCar class box with attributes and a method, and two car objects made from it, with notes on OOP ideas.
blocks.caption: Lists, tuples, indexing and slicing, modules and object-oriented programming (original diagram after topics 2.5 to 2.8).
blocks.long_description: Each item of a list has a position counted from 0 at the front and from -1 at the back, so fruits[0] is the first item and fruits[-1] the last; a slice such as fruits[1:4] takes the items from index 1 up to but not including 4. A module is a file of code that another file imports, and a package is a folder of related modules. A class is a template, such as ToyCar with colour, size and wheels and a describe method, and objects are individual cars made from it with their own values.

blocks.prompt: Class activity: for the string "Python Programming", what do s[7:] and s[-2:] give?

items: -1 is the last element; fruits[-4:-1] gives Banana, Cherry, Date; slicing works the same with negative indices.
